svg.title: An Easter gathering with room for everyone

text.tspan: Eggs are arranged together for a seasonal activity.
An Easter gathering with room for everyone
When we prepare an Easter gathering, a little care can make the experience better. Planning and
thinking about other people both help.
First, clear instructions help children join an activity safely. For example, we mark the egg-hunt area and
explain which places are out of bounds. This is a small thing that makes the day easier.
Second, recognizing different practices makes the gathering welcoming. For example, we ask families
which activities suit them instead of assuming a shared belief. We do not need a perfect day to do this
We can prepare an Easter gathering more easily when we prepare and notice other people. These
simple steps give us a useful place to start.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Your example. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two reasons are that clear
instructions help children join an activity safely and that recognizing different practices makes the gathering welcoming. One
example is that we mark the egg-hunt area and explain which places are out of bounds.)
